title: Balanced normalization of the scalar pullback mate on flat K-flat representatives
statement: Let X and Y be schemes and f:X→Y any morphism. Let φ:A→B be any homomorphism of commutative rings. Use the ordinary constant-ring module derived categories and pullback adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], scalar extension T and restriction r [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], the canonical restriction/pullback comparison b [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction], and the scalar/pullback comparison θ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. For every flat-term K-flat A-module complex P on Y, there exists a chain map t:f_A^*r_Y(T_Y P)→r_X(T_X(f_A^*P)) whose degree-i component sends the pullback unit of s tensor x to c_B(s) tensor the pullback unit of x, for every section s of B_Y and section x of P^i on every base-change object. Under the universal scalar-derived counits and exact-functor quotient comparisons, Q(t) agrees with b^{-1} followed by r_X(θ) at Q(P): the square in the attached Lean statement commutes. No boundedness, finiteness, properness or flatness of B over A is assumed.

proof.text: Construct the termwise ordinary comparison as the restriction/pullback map followed by restriction of the ordinary scalar/pullback conjugate. Prove its unit square by unit_conjugateEquiv_symm. The scalar-unit section formula gives the value on 1 tensor x; linearity gives the value on s tensor x. Naturality makes the degreewise maps a chain map t.

Prove the normalized scalar-unit formula for arbitrary complexes by choosing a K-flat resolution, applying pbcDerivedScalarAdjunction_exists on it, and cancelling its localized quasi-isomorphism using counit and unit naturality. The composition and natural-isomorphism factorization lemmas identify the termwise restriction/pullback square with its derived square. Normalize identity complex comparisons in the generic exact-functor calculation before specializing to sheaves, and use Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_symm to identify the specified derived inverse. Apply the generic normalized-mate transport theorem to this square and the ordinary scalar-unit equation, then identify the composite chain map degreewise with t.
